channel.title: Mercer Island Reporter - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Mercer Island Reporter (mi-reporter.com)

item.title: Rivian and Lucid could see direct-to-consumer car sales in WA
item.description: Legislation allowing luxury electric vehicle makers Rivian and Lucid to join rival Tesla in selling directly to Washington customers is on a fast track for action in Olympia.

item.title: DOH awards $2.5 million to local environmental organizations
item.description: Fifteen community-based and Tribal organizations throughout the state have been awarded funds.

item.title: Two residents were victims of identity theft involving tax forms | Mercer Island police blotter
Teams raise $7K-plus at MI Rowing Club ergathon
item.description: The Mercer Island Rowing Club held its inaugural Row for MI: Ergathon on March 1 at the local Orangetheory Fitness.

item.title: BECU to open new Mercer Island location
item.description: Washington credit union BECU expects to open a new Neighborhood Financial Center on Mercer Island in the late fall or winter of 2026, according to a March 4 press release.

item.title: MI author’s ‘Seattle Samurai’ receives Pacific Northwest book award
King County blocks construction of ICE detention centers
item.description: The King County Council approved an emergency one-year moratorium on March 3 that immediately blocks acceptance of permits for new or expanded detention facilities in unincorporated King County, preventing the siting of publicly or privately operated facilities, whether proposed as permanent or temporary uses.

item.title: MIHS Unified basketball squad scores second place at state
item.description: Athletes learn life skills during the season.

item.title: KC Council approves moratorium on detention centers
item.description: The King County Council approved a moratorium on detention centers in unincorporated King County as an effort to limit immigration enforcement in the county.

item.title: Revolutionary War reenactors visit students
item.description: Revolutionary War reenactors visited fifth-graders at West Mercer Elementary on March 2 in conjunction with a unit the students are doing on the Revolutionary War. Photo courtesy of the Mercer Island School District
